Instrumented-cc1 priority dump makes the printf-block residual a register-allocation question, not a scheduling one - and inverts s26/s27's 'arg4 must be inline' rule.

frontier.hypothesis: On the candidate.c chassis (named arg4 value local), a third scratch pseudo made live across sched1 positions 4-7 forces local-alloc's ascending scan past $v0 and $v1 onto $a0 for arg4's address, emitting target's arg4 chain without shortening the block.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc walks scratch hard regs in ascending number order (no REG_ALLOC_ORDER in mips.h). reg92 (arg4 address, def pos4 / dead pos7) currently overlaps only reg104 (arg5 address, pos6-9), so two registers suffice. A third overlapping scratch pseudo makes $v0 and $v1 both unavailable at reg92's scan. s27's m453 is a measured instance where the 3-scratch condition IS reached and target's arg4 chain is emitted byte-for-byte, but it drops build_insns to 90 and dbr then steals the sw 16($sp) into the printf delay slot.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep spellings that add a third scratch pseudo whose live range covers sched1 positions 4-7 WITHOUT removing an insn from the block: (a) arg5's VALUE named and assigned before arg4's statement so its pseudo spans the arg4 addu, (b) arg3's index named so its lbu is emitted before arg4's chain, (c) arg2 named as a value local so reg94 is born early and live to the a1 move. For each form do NOT score first: dump w.i.sched with tmp/grind/CD_datasync/s29/dmp.sh and count scratch pseudos live across the arg4 address pseudo's range, then check build_insns stays 91. The n*/x*/y*/z* families of s28 were classified by emitted window only; none was classified by this liveness predicate, which is the one that decides.

frontier.hypothesis: The dbr theft of sw 16($sp) into the printf delay slot - the cost that killed m453 and every 17-insn form - is separately blockable, so the 3-scratch condition and the 18-insn window are not actually in tension.
frontier.mechanism: s28 concluded the two halves of target are in direct tension because $a0 is free only when arg4's address pseudo dies early, and an early death moves the value load off the end of the block, letting reorg.c sink the stack store into the delay slot. The candidate.c dump shows a third configuration s28 never enumerated: the address pseudo dies early (pos7) while the VALUE pseudo reg86 stays live to the a3 move at the block end, so the block keeps its length. Whether dbr can still steal the store in that configuration is unmeasured.
frontier.next_probe: Take the m453 form (banked, tmp/grind/CD_datasync/s26/gen.py) and read its w.i.dbr dump to identify exactly which insn reorg.c sinks and why the sw is eligible; then test whether a spelling that keeps the arg4 VALUE pseudo live to the a3 move (rather than fusing the load into it) makes the store ineligible. Compare against candidate.c's w.i.dbr, where the jal printf delay slot is not filled by the store.

frontier.hypothesis: The twins CD_sync and CD_ready share this block, so the priority table and the scratch-liveness predicate transfer and one register-allocation answer closes three functions.
frontier.mechanism: CD_ready's ledger (s36/s46) records a byte-shape-identical do_timeout window and CD_sync s26 records the same {sll,addu,sll} -> jal debug_printf residual. The priorities measured here follow only from the argument shapes (four address chains, one stack arg, one constant fmt) and from calls.c's emission order, all of which the twins share.
frontier.next_probe: Run the BB2_PRIO_DEBUG dump (tmp/grind/CD_datasync/s29/prio.sh, retargeted) on CD_sync's and CD_ready's best banked forms and compare their printf-block priority tables and scratch-liveness counts against this one. If a twin's block already has three scratch pseudos live across its arg4 address range, that twin's C spelling is the answer for all three; if not, the difference in its table names the lever.
